paragraphs: Test-time adaptation uses unlabeled examples encountered during deployment to help a model cope with changing data. Many approaches require gradient calculations or repeated optimization, making adaptation expensive. ADAPT instead treats the problem as probabilistic inference: it updates a statistical description of each class and uses those descriptions to make predictions.

The method represents classes through gradually updated means and a covariance matrix shared across classes. Together, these quantities describe where class features tend to lie and how they vary. This formulation permits closed-form inference without training updates. To reduce potential bias in the resulting likelihoods, ADAPT adds lightweight regularization informed by CLIP priors and a bank of historical knowledge.

ADAPT needs neither the original training data nor access to the complete target dataset. It supports online adaptation as observations arrive, as well as transductive use. The authors report state-of-the-art performance across varied distribution shifts, alongside strong scalability and robustness. The contribution connects explicit modeling of class distributions with adaptation that avoids backpropagation.
neurips-2025-backpropagation-free-test-t.tldr: ADAPT adjusts class-distribution estimates during inference to handle distribution shifts without source data or gradient updates.

paragraphs: Learning new classes without retaining examples from earlier classes creates a difficult balance: a model must acquire new distinctions while preserving old knowledge. One common strategy freezes the feature extractor after the initial task. That protects existing representations, but does not explicitly teach the model how to distinguish newly introduced classes from previously learned ones.

CLOVER addresses the resulting overlap in class representations through two complementary mechanisms. Its confusion-driven self-supervised learning component focuses on classes that are especially easy to mistake for one another. By directing representation learning toward these difficult distinctions, it aims to make their features more separable. Its ensemble component progressively adjusts the weights used to combine diverse knowledge, further reducing overlap.

The authors report state-of-the-art results on the CIFAR100, TinyImageNet, and ImageNet-Subset benchmarks for learning without stored examples. These findings support targeting confusion between classes as part of the learning process. The approach combines better representation separation with a changing balance of ensemble contributions, addressing both how knowledge is represented and how it is combined.
neurips-2025-confusion-driven-self-super.tldr: CLOVER combines confusion-focused representation learning with a progressively weighted ensemble to learn new classes without retaining old examples.

paragraphs: People commonly associate the invented word bouba with rounded shapes and kiki with jagged shapes. This provides a concrete test of associations between language and vision. The paper revisits whether vision-and-language models show this pattern, focusing on two CLIP variants with different visual architectures: ResNet and Vision Transformer.

The researchers use two complementary evaluations modeled closely on human experiments. A prompt-based test measures model preferences through probabilities. Grad-CAM supplies an additional view by showing visual attention in shape-word matching tasks. Together, the methods examine both the models' choices and the image regions involved in those choices, allowing more than a single overall preference measurement.

Neither variant consistently displays the expected bouba-kiki association. ResNet favors round shapes, but that preference does not amount to reliably matching each word with its corresponding shape type. Comparisons with existing human results on the same task show markedly weaker associations in the models. The findings identify a specific gap between these CLIP variants and human cross-modal behavior, informing questions about how their internal representations connect visual and linguistic information.
neurips-2025-cross-modal-associations-in.tldr: Tests of two CLIP variants find that their shape-word associations do not consistently reproduce the human bouba-kiki effect.

paragraphs: Synthetic training data can help expand the material available for teaching language models to reason. However, generating many examples is less useful if they closely resemble a small seed collection or lack diversity. GRIP approaches this problem by organizing concepts extracted from seed examples into a knowledge graph that guides further data generation.

The graph supplies both explicit and implicit relationships between high-level concepts. GRIP uses these relationships to produce varied reasoning instructions at scale, with supervision from multiple open-source models supporting data quality. The method therefore makes the structure connecting concepts an active part of synthesis, rather than relying only on the original examples as direct generation templates.

Applied to mathematics, GRIP expands 7,500 seed reasoning samples into GRIP-MATH, containing 2.1 million question-answer pairs. The authors report greater diversity and scalability at lower cost than comparable synthesis approaches. Models trained on the resulting dataset substantially improve over their base models and outperform previous synthesis methods on mathematical reasoning benchmarks. These results support graph-guided generation as a way to expand both the amount and variety of useful reasoning data.
neurips-2025-grip-a-graph-based-reasonin.tldr: GRIP uses relationships in a concept graph to generate diverse mathematical reasoning data at scale and improve trained models.

paragraphs: Driving models that connect visual observations, language, and actions can struggle in unusual, unstructured situations. The paper identifies a shortage of targeted benchmarks as a major obstacle and introduces Impromptu VLA to address it. Its central contribution is a dataset designed around four categories of challenging unstructured driving scenarios.

The dataset contains more than 80,000 curated video clips selected from over two million source clips across eight open-source datasets. It combines planning-oriented questions and answers with action trajectories. This pairing provides material for examining what a model understands about a situation alongside the actions associated with it, connecting scene interpretation to driving decisions.

Models trained with the dataset improve closed-loop NeuroNCAP scores and collision rates, and approach state-of-the-art L2 accuracy for open-loop trajectory prediction on nuScenes. The question-answer suite also reveals improvements in perception, prediction, and planning for vision-language models. These findings show benefits across both action-oriented evaluation and diagnostic questioning. The project includes released code, data, and model weights to support further work on these driving situations.
neurips-2025-impromptu-vla-open-weights-.tldr: Impromptu VLA provides curated driving videos, planning questions, and trajectories that improve models on challenging driving evaluations.

paragraphs: Neural approaches to vehicle routing can learn useful decision policies on small problems, but their performance often deteriorates as problem size grows. The paper attributes this difficulty to a shift between training and testing distributions. A policy learned on 100-node instances may therefore be poorly suited to a much larger routing instance.

The proposed framework uses large language models to drive learning of a projection between those distributions. This projection is deployed to improve the existing routing model's scalability. The adaptation happens entirely during inference, so the approach does not require retraining the backbone neural network or jointly training it with the projection mechanism.

Experiments apply a backbone trained on 100-node problems to Traveling Salesman and Capacitated Vehicle Routing problems with up to 100,000 nodes across diverse distributions. The authors report superior performance in these large-scale settings. The contribution is a way to adapt an already trained solver when its deployment problems differ substantially in scale. Its stated results show that useful small-instance policies can be extended through test-time distribution adjustment.
neurips-2025-improving-generalization-of.tldr: An LLM-driven projection learned at inference time helps routing models trained on small instances tackle problems with up to 100,000 nodes.

paragraphs: Many fast Gaussian-splatting reconstruction methods place their 3D primitives along rays associated with input pixels. Overlapping views can consequently produce redundant primitives, while their placement remains constrained by the input images. The paper introduces a Fuse-and-Refine module that merges these initial representations in a common 3D space and produces more flexible refined primitives.

The module combines splats with a hierarchy of voxels, which are spatial cells at different resolutions. It aggregates local features into this hierarchy, then processes them with a sparse voxel transformer. Fusing multiple inputs this way reduces duplication and also allows successive video frames to contribute to a representation that retains information from earlier observations.

Trained on static scenes, the model generalizes to video without additional training, improving temporal coherence and handling occluded content. The authors report processing roughly 200,000 primitives in 15 milliseconds and state-of-the-art static and streaming reconstruction results. The full system runs at 15 frames per second with 350 milliseconds of delay on one H100 GPU. These distinct measurements describe both the module's processing speed and the broader reconstruction system's interactive performance.
neurips-2025-learning-efficient-fuse-and.tldr: A shared 3D fusion module removes redundant Gaussian primitives and improves static and streaming reconstruction using information across views and time.

paragraphs: Algorithmic recourse asks what feasible changes could turn an unfavorable model prediction into a favorable one. Searching for such changes after training can fail because a model optimized only for accuracy may offer no reasonable action. This paper builds recourse considerations into the learning of gradient boosted decision trees, a widely used model family for tabular data.

The proposed boosting algorithm accounts for a recourse guarantee while retaining the same time complexity as standard boosting algorithms. The authors also introduce a post-processing procedure that refines a trained model while respecting a recourse constraint. A PAC-style analysis provides a probabilistic theoretical treatment of the refined model's guarantee.

Experiments show that the method supplies reasonable actions for more instances than the baselines, without significantly harming predictive accuracy or computational efficiency. This makes recourse availability part of model construction rather than solely a question asked afterward. The combination of training and constrained refinement extends work on probabilistic recourse guarantees to boosted trees, connecting useful predictions with the availability of actions that can change them.
neurips-2025-learning-gradient-boosted-d.tldr: A recourse-aware boosting algorithm makes reasonable prediction-changing actions available for more instances while preserving accuracy and computational efficiency in experiments.

paragraphs: A reinforcement-learning agent working from images must distinguish information useful for its task from distracting visual noise. The paper argues that some denoising methods simplify this separation too aggressively. Once an observation is given, its task-relevant and task-irrelevant components can be conditionally dependent, so inferring one component can affect inference about the other.

CsDreamer addresses this issue through a world model called CsRSSM. Its collider structure explicitly represents the conditional dependence involved in denoising. A decoupling regularizer then balances the influence of that dependence. The goal is to infer a state representation containing the information needed for the task while accounting for how useful content and distractors interact during inference.

This inferred task-relevant state improves learning efficiency during model rollouts. Experiments show effective extraction of useful information and stronger performance than existing approaches in environments with complex noise interference. The results support treating the statistical relationship between signal and distraction as part of the denoising problem, with benefits extending from representation learning to the agent's subsequent learning process.
neurips-2025-leveraging-conditional-depe.tldr: CsDreamer models conditional dependence between useful visual information and distractors to improve world-model denoising and reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: Perspective understanding involves recognizing visual cues and reasoning about the spatial relationships they express. MMPerspective tests how well multimodal language models handle this distinction. It organizes ten tasks around perception, reasoning, and robustness, giving a structured way to examine whether apparent visual competence extends to consistent geometric understanding.

The benchmark contains 2,711 real and synthetic image instances with 5,083 question-answer pairs. Tasks include locating and counting vanishing points, identifying perspective types, understanding line relationships in three-dimensional space, and maintaining answers under transformations that preserve perspective. These different tests separate recognition of visible features from reasoning that combines spatial information or withstands changes in image presentation.

Evaluation of 43 models finds competence on relatively surface-level perception tasks alongside substantial difficulties with compositional reasoning and spatial consistency under perturbations. The analysis also identifies patterns associated with architecture and scale, and benefits from chain-of-thought prompting. The benchmark therefore provides a more specific diagnosis than an overall visual question-answering score: it reveals which parts of perspective understanding remain fragile in the evaluated systems.
neurips-2025-mmperspective-do-mllms-unde.tldr: MMPerspective finds that multimodal models handle basic perspective cues better than compositional geometric reasoning and robustness.

paragraphs: Choosing high-quality pretraining documents matters for language-model performance, but model-based selection has concentrated heavily on English. MuRating transfers quality judgments from English into a multilingual evaluator covering 17 languages. Its aim is to make data selection useful across the language mix required for multilingual training.

The framework first combines several English quality raters through comparisons between pairs of documents, learning unified quality scores. Translation carries these judgments into training examples for the multilingual evaluator. Training includes pairs within one language, across languages, and between parallel texts. This gives the evaluator several forms of comparative supervision rather than relying exclusively on separate scores assigned to individual documents.

The authors use MuRating to select balanced English and multilingual web-data subsets for pretraining LLaMA-architecture models with 1.2 billion and 7 billion parameters. They report higher average accuracy on English and multilingual evaluations than the named strong baselines. Further analyses find pairwise training more stable and robust than pointwise scoring. The findings connect multilingual quality selection with downstream gains in both English and other languages.
neurips-2025-murating-a-high-quality-dat.tldr: MuRating transfers English document-quality judgments into a 17-language evaluator that improves multilingual pretraining data selection.

paragraphs: Language models retain key and value information from earlier tokens in a cache used during generation. At long context lengths, moving and storing this cache becomes a major performance bottleneck. MUSTAFAR investigates unstructured sparsity, which removes individual cache elements, and reports sparsity as high as 70% without accuracy loss or fine-tuning in its evaluations.

The study finds that pruning by magnitude separately for each token works well for both key and value caches, outperforming prior structured schemes. Large outlier elements help explain the key-cache result. Magnitude pruning also works well for values despite their comparatively uniform distribution. This makes a relatively simple selection rule effective across both cache components.

To turn sparsity into practical acceleration, the authors develop a bitmap storage format and an attention kernel that computes directly over compressed caches with arbitrary sparsity patterns. Faster memory-bound computation compensates for runtime pruning and compression costs. The reported cache footprint reaches 45% of dense inference, with throughput improvements up to 2.23 times. The contribution combines an effective pruning strategy with the machinery needed to benefit from it during decoding.
neurips-2025-mustafar-promoting-unstruct.tldr: MUSTAFAR combines individual-element KV-cache pruning with compressed attention computation to reduce memory use and accelerate language-model decoding.

paragraphs: Reconstructing an unknown signal from a noisy linear measurement can involve many plausible answers. Posterior sampling seeks samples that reflect both prior knowledge of the signal and the observed measurement. The paper asks when this can be done efficiently using an approximate prior, with applications including inpainting, deblurring, and MRI reconstruction.

Because approximate posterior sampling is computationally intractable in general, the analysis focuses on distributions with local or global log-concavity. In this setting, Langevin dynamics works with exact scores, which describe how log density changes. Its sensitivity to estimated scores is problematic: the existing requirement controls error tails through a moment-generating-function bound. Unconditional diffusion sampling can succeed under a weaker squared-error condition, but does not itself resolve conditioning on measurements.

The authors prove that combining diffusion models with annealed Langevin dynamics enables polynomial-time conditional sampling with an L4 score-error bound. This controls the fourth moment of estimation error rather than requiring the stronger tail condition. The result establishes a more error-tolerant sampling guarantee within the stated log-concavity regime, without claiming to remove the general computational hardness.
neurips-2025-posterior-sampling-by-combi.tldr: Under log-concavity assumptions, diffusion combined with annealed Langevin dynamics permits polynomial-time posterior sampling using an L4 score-error bound.

paragraphs: Coarse-to-fine speech synthesis first produces a rough representation and then improves it. In conventional flow-matching systems, the rough representation conditions a generation process that begins from noise. Shallow Flow Matching changes how that initial output is used: it constructs a state partway along the flow path, giving refinement a more advanced starting point.

During training, an orthogonal projection method adaptively determines where that intermediate state should sit along the path. A construction based on a single-segment piecewise flow supports this formulation. At inference, generation begins from the constructed intermediate state, concentrating computation on the later part of the transformation instead of traversing the full path from pure noise.

The authors integrate this mechanism into multiple text-to-speech systems using a lightweight prediction head. Experiments show consistent improvements in speech naturalness under both objective measurements and subjective evaluation. They also report substantial inference acceleration when adaptive-step ODE solvers are used. The findings suggest that a coarse generator can contribute more directly to refinement by providing its starting state, improving speech quality while reducing computation in the evaluated solver setting.
neurips-2025-shallow-flow-matching-for-c.tldr: Shallow Flow Matching starts speech refinement partway along a generation path, improving naturalness and accelerating inference with adaptive-step solvers.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks commonly update each node using information from nearby nodes. This local structure is useful, but distant information can become compressed as it travels, node representations can become overly similar, and some distinctions remain hard to express. The paper adds global feature information to standard graph networks to address these linked difficulties.

The proposed Sketched Random Features are randomized global embeddings of node features. They are designed to be unique and sensitive to distance without depending on graph topology. Injecting these embeddings gives the network access to information beyond what its ordinary local aggregation supplies. The authors use both analysis and experiments to show how these properties alleviate oversquashing, oversmoothing, and limits on expressive power.

Across real-world graph-learning tasks, the added features consistently improve performance over baseline graph networks. The method can be used on its own or alongside existing enhancements such as graph positional encodings. Its contribution is therefore a feature augmentation that helps standard architectures capture long-range dependencies while remaining compatible with other approaches to improving graph representations.
neurips-2025-sketch-augmented-features-i.tldr: Randomized global feature sketches help graph neural networks capture distant information and improve performance alongside existing representation techniques.

paragraphs: Knowing where an object is does not fully specify how a robot should manipulate it. Orientation also matters, especially when actions require control over both position and rotation. SoFar introduces semantic orientation, describing meaningful object directions through language, such as a USB connector's insertion direction or the direction of a cup's handle.

This description avoids defining orientation through predefined reference frames or object templates. To support it, the authors construct OrienText300K, a dataset of three-dimensional objects annotated with semantic orientations, and develop PointSO for zero-shot orientation prediction. The SoFar framework then integrates this information into vision-language agents, connecting spatial reasoning about orientation with generated robotic actions.

Experiments report zero-shot success rates of 48.7% on Open6DOR and 74.9% on SIMPLER-Env. These results support the usefulness and generalization of the framework in the evaluated manipulation settings. The contribution provides a connection between language that names an object's meaningful directions and the orientation information required for six-degree-of-freedom manipulation, expanding spatial reasoning beyond relationships between object locations.
neurips-2025-sofar-language-grounded-ori.tldr: SoFar expresses object orientation through meaningful language descriptions and uses them to support zero-shot spatial reasoning and robotic manipulation.

paragraphs: Participatory budgeting selects projects using public preferences and a limited budget. This paper studies the incentives of project proposers when they can choose the prices of their proposals. It assumes approval votes are already fixed and known, so the strategic decision concerns project pricing while voter preferences remain unchanged.

Each proposer wants the highest possible price that still allows their project to be selected. Prices must also cover a minimum delivery cost. These requirements create a tradeoff: raising a price is desirable for the proposer, but selection depends on the budgeting rule and the competing proposals. The analysis considers AV/Cost, Phragmen, and the Method of Equal Shares.

The theoretical question is whether these pricing games admit pure Nash equilibria: stable price choices where no proposer can improve their outcome through an individual change. The paper also studies cost selection experimentally using real participatory-budgeting election data. Its contribution examines project costs as strategic choices, making the funding rule's interaction with proposer incentives an explicit subject of analysis.
neurips-2025-strategic-cost-selection-in.tldr: The paper studies stable strategic project pricing under three participatory-budgeting rules when approval votes are fixed and known.

paragraphs: Generating a hand interacting with an object requires visual appearance and physical motion to agree. Existing motion methods often depend on predefined object models and laboratory motion data, while video methods can prioritize convincing pixels at the expense of plausible movement. SViMo generates video and motion together through a synchronized diffusion process.

The framework combines visual priors with dynamic constraints. Adaptive modulation aligns semantic, appearance, and motion features, while three-dimensional full attention models relationships within and across these feature types. A vision-aware interaction diffusion model then produces explicit 3D interaction sequences from the synchronized outputs and feeds them back into the process, creating a feedback loop between generated representations.

The architecture avoids dependence on predefined object models or explicit pose guidance and improves agreement between video and motion. Experiments report stronger visual fidelity and dynamic plausibility than state-of-the-art approaches, together with generalization to unseen real-world scenarios. The findings support joint generation and feedback as ways to make the appearance of an interaction more consistent with its underlying movement.
neurips-2025-svimo-synchronized-diffusio.tldr: SViMo jointly generates hand-object videos and 3D motion through synchronized diffusion and feedback, improving their consistency and physical plausibility.

paragraphs: A visually convincing digital avatar can still miss subtle facial geometry. The paper connects this difficulty to similar skin colors and an approximation used when projecting Gaussian primitives into images. That approximation does not adequately capture depth-related shear under perspective, weakening reconstruction when fine geometric changes produce only subtle appearance differences.

TGA introduces a perspective-aware Gaussian transformation that models deformation over time together with spatial projection. It uses Jacobian-guided adaptive deformation within a homogeneous formulation to maintain sensitivity to color and consistency with geometry. The purpose is to make the representation respond more faithfully to small facial variations as the avatar moves.

The framework also includes an incremental procedure for extracting meshes frame by frame. A dynamic bounding-volume hierarchy represents relationships among points; pivoting identifies active points, which are then re-triangulated into a surface. Experiments report superior geometric accuracy. Together, the transformation and extraction method address both the fidelity of the dynamic Gaussian representation and the efficient recovery of explicit surfaces from it.
neurips-2025-tga-true-to-geometry-avatar.tldr: TGA combines perspective-aware Gaussian deformation with incremental mesh extraction to improve the geometric accuracy of dynamic avatars.

paragraphs: Sampling from an unnormalized distribution can require many computational steps that depend on earlier results. This paper studies how many sequential rounds are needed when the target distribution is not log-concave. It measures sampling accuracy through relative Fisher information and focuses on adaptive complexity, the part of computation that cannot simply be performed simultaneously.

For a target relative Fisher information of at most epsilon squared, the proposed algorithm reduces the sequential-round bound from O(d²/epsilon⁴) to O(d/epsilon²), where d is dimension. It achieves this through parallelism using a diagonally parallelized Picard iteration. The result concerns the number of dependent rounds, so its stated improvement specifically describes how the computation can be organized across parallel work.

The authors also establish a matching optimality result in a particular regime of large epsilon. Their lower bound comes from reducing the problem of finding stationary points to this sampling setting. This provides both an improved algorithm and a boundary on further improvements within that regime, while leaving the optimality claim explicitly tied to the stated accuracy range.
neurips-2025-the-adaptive-complexity-of-.tldr: A parallel sampling algorithm reduces sequential-round complexity for controlling relative Fisher information and is optimal in a specified large-epsilon regime.

paragraphs: Time-series forecasting becomes difficult when the distribution of observations changes over time. TimeEmb approaches this problem by separating persistent patterns from changing ones. The motivation is that learning both together can blur the distinction between stable structure and short-term variation, reducing forecasting performance when the data distribution shifts.

The framework assigns the two components to different mechanisms. A global embedding module learns representations that capture patterns persisting across time series. An efficient frequency-domain filter handles the time-varying component, drawing inspiration from full-spectrum signal analysis. This division gives stable and changing information distinct processing paths while treating them as complementary parts of the same forecasting problem.

Experiments on real-world datasets show better performance than state-of-the-art baselines while using fewer computational resources. Quantitative and qualitative analyses support the value of separating the components. The framework can also improve existing forecasting methods through simple integration. The findings therefore present static-dynamic separation as both a forecasting approach in its own right and a lightweight addition to other methods.
neurips-2025-timeemb-a-lightweight-stati.tldr: TimeEmb separates persistent and changing time-series patterns to improve forecasting accuracy with lower computational demands.

paragraphs: A metalearner uses experience across related tasks to learn a new task from fewer examples. This paper provides a theoretical analysis of that ability for a simplified transformer trained by gradient descent. At test time, the transformer adapts through examples placed in its context, without further parameter training.

The analysis considers linear classification tasks generated by class-conditional Gaussian mixtures. Across tasks, the mean vectors lie within a shared k-dimensional subspace of a d-dimensional space. This shared structure is the source of potential efficiency: prior training can help a model use task relationships that are unavailable to a learner seeing only the new task's examples.

After training on sufficiently many tasks, the transformer needs approximately k/R⁴ in-context examples, up to logarithmic factors, where R represents test-time signal strength. A learner restricted to the new context requires a lower bound proportional to d/R⁴. The transformer's performance nearly matches a learner given the shared subspace exactly. The result demonstrates near-optimal metalearning under this structured classification model, with the benefit expressed through intrinsic dimension rather than ambient dimension.
neurips-2025-transformers-are-almost-opt.tldr: For Gaussian classification tasks sharing a low-dimensional subspace, a trained simplified transformer nearly matches an optimal metalearner's example efficiency.

paragraphs: A model can use both local texture and the arrangement of object parts, so measuring a preference for shape over texture may hide its actual shape-recognition ability. This paper introduces the Configural Shape Score to test that ability directly. Its object-anagram pairs preserve local texture while rearranging parts to depict different object categories.

Recognizing both images requires sensitivity to their different overall configurations. Across 86 vision models, the score reveals a wide range of abilities, with self-supervised and language-aligned transformers among the strongest. Mechanistic tests connect high scores to long-range interactions: restricting attention disrupts performance, and representation analyses reveal a transition from local to global coding around the middle of the networks.

A BagNet control remains at chance despite receptive fields spanning patch boundaries, supporting the authors' rejection of border-based shortcuts in that control. The score also predicts performance on other shape-dependent evaluations, including foreground bias and robustness to spectral changes and noise. The findings motivate evaluating global shape competence directly and suggest that integrating local texture with global configuration may support more robust vision.
neurips-2025-visual-anagrams-reveal-hidd.tldr: Visual anagrams reveal large differences in models' global shape recognition and connect stronger performance to long-range visual integration.

paragraphs: When successive generative models train on data produced by earlier models, errors can accumulate into model collapse. This paper studies that feedback process for maximum likelihood estimation in a setting where synthetic examples are gradually added to the original training set. Keeping the original data is part of the setup, even as its share becomes smaller.

Under standard assumptions resembling those used for classical consistency and asymptotic normality of maximum likelihood estimates, the authors establish finite-sample bounds showing that collapse can be avoided. This remains possible even when the fraction of real data tends toward zero. The result makes the statistical assumptions and accumulation process central to understanding when repeated synthetic-data training remains stable.

The paper also proves that consistency of maximum likelihood estimation alone is insufficient. Without additional assumptions, collapse can happen arbitrarily quickly despite retaining the original examples. These counterexamples show why preservation of real data does not by itself establish stability. Together, the positive bounds and failure constructions explain how different conclusions about collapse can arise under different assumptions.
neurips-2025-when-models-dont-collapse-o.tldr: Iterative maximum likelihood training can avoid collapse under suitable assumptions, but retaining original data and ordinary consistency alone do not suffice.

paragraphs: Reinforcement-learning policies often struggle when evaluation environments have different parameters from their training environments. Training across many contexts can help, but collecting that experience may be impractical. This paper studies how structure in the way environments vary can improve generalization when training data comes from very few contexts, including a single one.

The analysis assumes contextual Markov decision processes whose transition and reward functions have regularity with respect to context parameters. The authors introduce a context-enhanced Bellman equation and show that it gives a first-order approximation to the Q function learned across multiple contexts. This connects single-context learning to an approximation of the value information that broader context training would provide.

They then derive context sample enhancement, a data-augmentation method that efficiently approximates the new equation in deterministic control environments. Simulation experiments demonstrate its potential to improve generalization. The theoretical and practical contributions are linked: regularity supports the approximation, and the augmentation procedure makes that approximation usable in the stated control setting. The result offers a route toward context generalization with reduced demands for diverse training experience.
neurips-2025-zero-shot-context-generaliz.tldr: A context-enhanced Bellman equation and derived augmentation method improve the prospects for reinforcement-learning generalization from few training contexts.
